chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Toots Mondello: session man and a rumour of his death
summary: Freeman and Dance discuss Mondello as a studio saxophonist who studied composition, and Dance's unconfirmed report that he died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Toots Mondello, the great -- now, he has become quite a composer, having studied some 20 years with Creston, I believe.
Toots just died not long ago.
I didn't know.
Well, I think so. Benny and I talked on the phone not long ago and I think Toots just died.
I didn't hear a word about it.
Now, don't take that for gospel, but I am almost sure.
I am sorry to hear that, I didn't hear a word of it. Because he was a brilliant musician.
Yes, simply gorgeous sound.
Toots was not a jazz man, but a marvelous session man, beautiful musician and had studied all those years to become a composer.
Had he? I didn't know.
Well, I am quite sure he had
written several things years, but I did not see much of Toots, you see, after I left. I saw him a couple of times --

I may be wrong and you must might check with somebody, but I think I heard it this year, because I said to Stanley, 'Oh, that's very sad,' because he is a wonderful musician and then Benny and I were talking on the phone the other day, about something, and Benny said to me, 'You saw that didn't you?' I think Benny went to the funeral.
Now, I could be wrong, but --
Are you speaking about Benny Goodman?
Yeah.
Oh, well, then if Benny went to the funeral.
I cannot think I would confuse Toots with anybody else.
There was only one Toots Mondello
I thought you might have seen that in something, but you might check.
I hadn't heard a word about it.
So just don't take it for gospel, but I think I am right.
